title: Medium PNT by instantiating GenStrengthPNT at exponents 9, 9
intent: Prove the medium prime-number theorem ψ(x) = x + O(x exp(−c (log x)^(1/10))) by stating and proving the stronger general form once — GenStrengthPNT over arbitrary exponents n₁, n₂ — then specialising n₁ = n₂ = 9 through LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHolo99, leaving only a simplification of 1/(1+9) to 1/10.

parent.name: MediumPNT
parent.statement:
theorem MediumPNT : ∃ c > 0,
    (ψ - id) =O[atTop]
      fun (x : ℝ) ↦ x * Real.exp (-c * (Real.log x) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10))

children.name: GenStrengthPNT
children.statement:
lemma GenStrengthPNT {n₁ n₂ : ℝ}
  (LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHolo : LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHoloGenProp n₁ n₂)
  (n₁_pos : 0 < n₁) (n₂_pos : 0 < n₂) : ∃ c > 0,
  (ψ - id) =O[atTop]
    fun (x : ℝ) ↦ x * Real.exp (-c * (Real.log x) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (1 + n₁)))
children.closed_by: its own 521-line proof (lines 3611-4131): it obtains I1Bound … I9Bound, SmoothedChebyshevClose, SmoothedChebyshevPull1/2 and MellinOfSmooth1cExplicit, then closes with a calc chain of inequalities ending in `rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg]`

applicability.goal_shape: a concrete theorem whose statement is the image of a general theorem under a substitution of its parameters (here the exponent 1/(1+n₁) becomes 1/10 by n₁ = 9), with the general theorem already proved over the parameters
applicability.use_when: the hard part depends on the parameters only through a proven general bound, and the instantiation is discharged by unification plus cheap arithmetic (linarith, ring_nf)
applicability.avoid_when: the concrete instance needs an argument the general proof does not cover, or the general lemma's side conditions (here 0 < n₁, 0 < n₂) cannot be closed by automation

claims.claim: The parent MediumPNT closes in two tactic lines that instantiate GenStrengthPNT at n₁ = n₂ = 9 and simplify the exponent: `have := GenStrengthPNT LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHolo99 (by linarith) (by linarith); ring_nf at this` then `simpa only [gt_iff_lt, one_div, neg_mul] using this`.
claims.evidence: https://github.com/AlexKontorovich/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/blob/2c476fa6441c607096d93c8fc7ac0a227a655dae/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/MediumPNT.lean#L4142-L4146; the file is compiled by .github/workflows/build.yml (lean-action, build-args :blueprint) on pushes to main

claims.claim: Shape measured on the copied file: 2 direct lemmas (GenStrengthPNT, LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHolo99), 2 lines of glue (lines 4145-4146), child proof lines [521, 1] (GenStrengthPNT 3611-4131, LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHolo99 3501), and depth 2 along MediumPNT → LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHolo99 → LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHoloGen.

The authors state the general form first: the GenStrengthPNT blueprint says 'Assuming a bound of the form of Definition \ref{LogDerivZetaHasBound}, we have that ∑_{n ≤ x} Λ(n) = x + O(x exp(−c (log x)^{1/(1+n₁)})).'

No sorry, admit or axiom closes any of the lemmas: a grep for these tokens over the copied MediumPNT.lean and ZetaBounds.lean returns nothing, and the file ends with the author's own check `#print axioms MediumPNT` (line 4148).
claims.evidence: grep -nE '\bsorry\b|\badmit\b|\baxiom\b' over the two copied files returned no matches; https://github.com/AlexKontorovich/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/blob/2c476fa6441c607096d93c8fc7ac0a227a655dae/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/MediumPNT.lean#L4148

claims.claim: The same generalise-then-instantiate move runs a second time one level down in ZetaBounds.lean: LogDerivZetaHolcLargeTGen (general n) is instantiated at n = 9 by LogDerivZetaHolcLargeT9, and LogDerivZetaBndUnif99 : LogDerivZetaBndUnifGenProp 9 9 is the bound LogDerivZetaBoundedAndHolo99 consumes.

metrics.how_counted: parent statement = lines 4142-4144 and proof = lines 4145-4146 of the copied PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/MediumPNT.lean; children = the two named lemmas the glue cites directly

consequences: The move leaves two side conditions of the general lemma to discharge at the instantiation site — here 0 < 9 twice, closed by `linarith` — plus a normalisation of the exponent (1/(1+9) → 1/10) closed by `ring_nf`/`simpa`. If the concrete instance changes a parameter in a way the general proof's hypotheses do not cover, the instantiation fails; the general lemma must be stated so that its hypotheses are exactly what the concrete case can supply.
